newsitem.title: ITALY: Importers see glimmer of hope for Italy car market.
newsitem.headline: Importers see glimmer of hope for Italy car market.

text.p: Better than expected Italian new car registrations in December coupled with prospects for new sales from the Italian government's car incentive scheme have opened up a "glimmer of hope" for the domestic auto market, the Italian association of car importers Unrae said.

Transport Ministry data issued on Friday showed new car registrations in 1996 rose 0.34 percent to 1.74 million units and for December alone rose 12.14 percent to 111,000 against forecasts for a rise of 102,000-105,000.
Unrae said in a statement that the December figures clearly benefited from strong advertising campaigns by manufacturers.

But it said the data should be reinforced this year by the government's new scheme to boost new car sales by giving motorists cash bonuses for trading in cars over 10 years old for scrapping in exchange for buying new models.
"We should see a resulting acceleration in car demand but for this to be maintained we will still need to see a revitalisation of household consumption," Unrae said.
